philosophers.name: Plotinus
philosophers.pico_relevance: Central to Pico's metaphysics, ontology of emanation, soul-matter relation, and mystical union
philosophers.notes: Pico's *Heptaplus* and *Conclusions* draw heavily on Plotinian henology

philosophers.name: Porphyry (Malchos)

key_works.title: Sententiae ad Intelligibilia (Launching Points for the Intelligible Realm)
key_works.notes: Main systematic work; heavily used in medieval philosophy

key_works.title: Isagoge (Introduction)
key_works.notes: Intro to Aristotle's *Categories*; became standard logic text

key_works.title: On Abstinence (De Abstinentia)
key_works.notes: Ethics and theurgy; Pico cites for demonology

philosophers.pico_relevance: Demonology, daemon hierarchy, theurgy, substance/essence debates, ethical theory
philosophers.notes: Pico's daemon cosmology and theurgic theses often cite Porphyry's *On Abstinence*

philosophers.name: Iamblichus of Apamea
philosophers.period: Late Neoplatonism, founder of Syrian school

key_works.title: On the Pythagorean Life
key_works.notes: Fragments on Pythagorean symbolism and practice

philosophers.pico_relevance: Foundational for Pico's theurgic theses, divine names, daemons, ritual efficacy
philosophers.notes: Iamblichus systematized theurgy; Pico's condemned propositions include theurgic claims

philosophers.name: Proclus Lycaeus

key_works.title: Elements of Theology (Stoicheiosis Theologike)
key_works.notes: Most systematic Neoplatonic work; heavily cited in medieval scholasticism

key_works.title: Theologia Platonica
key_works.notes: Extensive commentary on Plato; medieval reception crucial

key_works.title: Commentary on the Parmenides
key_works.notes: Dense ontological work; influences medieval henology

philosophers.pico_relevance: Henology, triadic logic, henads as divine names, medieval transmission via Pseudo-Dionysius
philosophers.notes: Allen is the expert on Proclus in Pico; *Elements of Theology* is most cited Neoplatonic text in medieval scholasticism

philosophers.name: Chaldean Oracles (Logia Chaldaica)
philosophers.dates: c. 2nd century CE (attributed to Julianus the Chaldean & son)

key_works.title: Oracles (Fragments)
key_works.notes: Only fragmentary; cited through Porphyry, Iamblichus, Proclus

philosophers.pico_relevance: Divine names, theurgic practice, fire-theology, Pico's prisca theologia
philosophers.notes: Quasi-scriptural status in late Neoplatonism; crucial for Pico's theurgic magic

philosophers.name: Nicomachus of Gerasa

key_works.title: Introduction to Arithmetic (Arithmetica)
key_works.notes: Pythagorean numerology; standard medieval arithmetic text

philosophers.pico_relevance: Number mysticism, Kabbalah-Pythagorean parallels in Pico's numeric theses
philosophers.notes: Pico often conflates Nicomachus with Kabbalah on number; check for synthesis theses

philosophers.name: Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite

key_works.title: Divine Names (De Divinis Nominibus)
key_works.notes: Neoplatonic henology in Christian theological garb

philosophers.pico_relevance: Medieval transmission of Neoplatonism; Pico's angel/daemon cosmology mediated by Pseudo-Dionysius
philosophers.notes: Key filter for Pico's reception of Proclean henology and angelic theses

philosophers.name: Apuleius of Madauros

key_works.title: On the God of Socrates (De Deo Socratis)
key_works.notes: Daemons and intermediaries in Platonic cosmology

philosophers.pico_relevance: Daemon classification, Pico's demonology, magic within Platonic framework
philosophers.notes: Pico uses Apuleius on daemons to authorize Renaissance magic theory

related_figures.name: Marsilio Ficino
related_figures.pico_relevance: Shared Neoplatonic sources; Pico's Neoplatonism shaped by Ficino's transmission

related_figures.name: Thomas Aquinas
related_figures.pico_relevance: Pico synthesizes Aquinas + Neoplatonism on emanation, substance, being

metadata.note: This index covers major Neoplatonist and related figures relevant to Pico900 commentary. Use this as reference when identifying which philosopher(s) a thesis invokes.
